$comment: The fix-and-recheck preconditions for /finalise Step 8a (task.128). This file is the ONE definition: finalise-fix-and-recheck.mjs evaluates it, the Step 6 decision table and the DoD checklist's matrix cite it by id, and tests/finalise-fix-and-recheck.test.mjs (beside this file) pins the ids so a sixth cannot be added silently and none can be dropped. ALL must hold; any one false is the existing Step 8 halt.

preconditions.statement: the finding's `severity` is `low`, read from the agent's YAML — a finding that carries no severity is NOT low
preconditions.why: The path exists for a one-line, fail-closed defect. A medium or high finding is the halt it always was, and a missing severity is a question the agent did not answer, not a low one.

preconditions.statement: the fix is exactly one commit
preconditions.why: One commit is one thing to revert, one head to re-read CI on, and one diff a reader can hold in view.

preconditions.statement: every path the fix touches is listed in the work item's Files Summary (task §7) or File List (story) — or is the work item's own document, named by `documentPath`, which is inside its own scope by construction
preconditions.why: A fix outside the task's own file set is new scope, and scope is what QA reviewed; a fix inside it is a correction to what QA already covered.

preconditions.statement: a named test goes red when the fix is reverted, and the run that showed it is recorded to a file the evaluator opens (mutationProof.run: non-empty, names the test, carries a red marker)
preconditions.why: A fix with no red-on-revert test is a change nothing holds; the next edit can undo it silently.

preconditions.statement: no medium-or-higher finding is open in any section, and no other DoD section is FAIL
preconditions.why: The path re-runs the ONE failed section's reproduction, not the four agents. That is sound only when nothing else was wrong — a second open finding means the tree is not the one the other sections judged.
